title: KV whale: memory fissure hotfix + hosted failover playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated experienced sustained GPU OOM waves starting 2025-02-09. Root cause is a KV-cache growth/leak pattern combined with allocator fragmentation that prevents arena reclamation under long-lived multi-session workloads. The kv-journal accumulated tombstones and foreign journal pointers that prevented incremental compaction; meanwhile the allocator kept fragmenting large arenas for ephemeral tensors. Net result: gradual memory cliff, high GPU resident pages, and OOMs for chat workloads longer than ~8k tokens.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running chat session against model rdx-13b with long context and repeated tool calls (simulate streaming chunk responses).
2) Interleave high-concurrency ephemeral embedding calls from separate tenants to force KV journal churn and tombstone creation.
3) Observe cumulative KV index size growth in /metrics and escalating GPU resident memory for the node in ~30-90 minutes.
4) Verify allocator free lists show many small fragments and very few reclaimable arenas via /debug/allocator_stats.
5) Reproduce locally with a dedicated-1 GPU workload and the test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tests/oom-fuzz (internal).
investigation_notes: Observed correlated spikes in kv_journal_tombstones_total and gpu_resident_bytes for affected nodes.
Heap profiler snapshots show many small allocations pinned to arenas reserved for session caches; arenas not returned to system due to missing coalescer fast-path under high tombstone counts.

KV index compactor was not invoked when journal growth rate exceeded threshold because compactor threshold logic expected periodic low-load pauses (which didn't occur under continuous streaming workloads).
Customer traces (support-ACME-2241, support-Orbis-399) show ramp from healthy to OOM in 45-120 minutes depending on concurrency.
Memory fragmentation regret metric added: allocator_frag_ratio rose above 0.78 before OOMs.
No evidence of data corruption on disk; KV lookups remained correct, but in-memory metadata grew without bound.
Reproduced in dedicated staging by lifting journal_compaction_threshold to emulate heavy churn; confirmed fix candidate reduced resident bytes by ~28% in stress test.
Potential risk: aggressive compaction could introduce brief CPU spikes and latency blips; we needed a controlled rollout and circuit breaker.
Related signals: increased rate of session re-creation (session_evictions_total) and higher RPC latency due to blocking compactor thread prior to fix.
mitigation_plan: 1) Emergency daemon patch (hotfix): enable background incremental KV compaction triggered by journal_size_delta rather than idle window. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428)
2) Allocator coalescer fast-path: return freed arenas to OS when contiguous free runs exceed 1MB and fragmentation ratio above 0.6. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1431)
3) Short-term rolling restart playbook for severely affected hosted nodes to reclaim stuck arenas (automated via orchestrator job restart-kv-reclaim).
4) Introduce backpressure: reject new high-memory sessions from tenants triggering growth above tenant_kv_limit until compaction completes.
5) Add temporary throttling rule in front of hosted burst pool to move long context sessions to dedicated fallback pool when available.
6) Customer communication: send interim notice and mitigation steps to impacted accounts; opened support threads: support-ACME-2241, support-Orbis-399.
7) Monitoring: add alert kvcache_journal_growth_rate > 5MB/min for 10min and allocator_frag_ratio > 0.7.
8) Escalation: require on-call runtime + infra until rollout confirms stability.
rollout_plan: Canary: Deploy hotfix to 8 nodes in hosted-us-east-1 serving non-critical traffic (00:00-04:00 UTC low-traffic window).
Verification: Run the internal oom-fuzz suite and validate kvcache_journal_tombstones_total declines and gpu_resident_bytes stabilizes.
Gradual increase: Expand to 25% of hosted pool over 6 hours, then 50% if no regressions for 2 hours.
Dedicated: Offer hotfix as immediate upgrade to customer-dedicated pools; require approval from Dedicated ops for on-prem changes.
Private deployments: Publish patch notes and backport instructions; provide an opt-in package for air-gapped installs and an enterprise support assisted upgrade path.
Rollback criteria: any sustained increase in tail latency (p95 request latency +15% over baseline for >15min) or a new increase in cpu_compactor_time > 200% triggers rollback.
Automated jobs: orchestrator job to traffic-shift 5% of long-context sessions to fallback pool during rollout window to minimize customer-visible OOMs.
qa_acceptance_criteria: No regression in existing unit and integration tests; new unit tests covering compaction-trigger behavior added.
Stress tests: runtime/stress/long-context must run 4 hours without OOM and with stable allocator_frag_ratio < 0.65.
Canary telemetry must show 25%+ reduction in journal growth rate and resident GPU memory stabilization within 30 minutes post-deploy.
No auth/security impact; smoke SSO and RBAC checks pass for private and dedicated upgrades.
Customer verification: at least one impacted customer (ACME) confirms no further OOMs in their replica environment after upgrade.

postmortem_actions: 1) Ship runtime-1.22 with compactor improvements and allocator coalescer next minor release.
2) Add integration test that combines long-context streaming + high embedding churn to catch future regressions.
3) Update runbook: automated traffic-shift playbook and clearer tenant_kv_limit guidance.
4) Instrument per-tenant KV growth and surface in Console with tenant_kv_alerts.
5) Investigate long-term allocator redesign to avoid reliance on ad-hoc coalescer thresholds.
6) Schedule a cross-team blameless postmortem review session (runtime, infra, product) within 2 weeks.
